A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSEarth research, with matching construction methods, datasets, and tasks. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations and post-training results in Tables 2–4, plus caption ablations, reasoning experiments, and human evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original evaluations and human studies, and reports additional model comparisons and subdiscipline results in Tables 4–5 and 13–16.

M1.justification: Refined-caption generation, three-phase multi-agent voting, expert filtering, and instruction-tuning/GRPO procedures remain unchanged. The shortened prompt documentation does not establish a change to the underlying generation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain five Earth spheres, eight disciplines, 66 subdisciplines, and captioning, MCQ, and open-ended tasks. The 300-question specialized mini-benchmark already exists in v2; the new subdiscipline tables disaggregate existing coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds Qwen3-VL-32B, GLM-4.1V-Thinking, full Intern-S1, GPT-5.2, and Gemini-3-Flash to the MCQ comparison; Gemini-3-Flash also enters captioning and open-ended QA. Qwen2.5-VL-32B and GPT-4o-mini disappear from captioning/open-ended comparisons, and Claude-3.5-Haiku from captioning. Their MCQ results remain available elsewhere in v3.

E3.justification: The reported captioning/open-ended metric suite narrows from ROUGE-1/2/L to ROUGE-L, and Section 4.2 removes the stated use of a factual-entailment classifier. Splits and established evaluation designs remain unchanged; the MCQ similarity fallback is retained in Appendix J.2. These reporting changes do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Tables 13–16 add performance breakdowns across 24 subdisciplines, extending the existing broad-domain analysis to show variation within disciplines. Original-caption ablations, CoT/voting experiments, human evaluations, and case studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The four-annotator, 160-question metric validation, Spearman correlations, Krippendorff agreement, and three-expert averaging already appear in v2. V3 introduces no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: New MCQ results include Gemini-3-Flash at 68.82% and Intern-S1 at 65.63%, changing rankings above the retained 63.54% tuned baseline. Gemini-2.5-Flash-Thinking's reported OE-Eval changes from 46.49% to 52.40%, and Gemini-2.5-Pro-Thinking's open-ended ROUGE-L from 38.38 to 40.39, without an explained protocol change. Subdiscipline scores are added, while ROUGE-1/2 results and the aggregate correlation column are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The mathematical rules described for similarity filtering, voting thresholds, and human-rating aggregation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Despite the revised title and opening prose, both claim a graduate-level Earth-science benchmark, context-enriched captions, combined automated/expert validation, and training resources that improve post-trained models. The additional comparisons do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 Appendix A newly acknowledges possible underrepresentation of niche or highly specialized geoscience subfields. Interpretations of the reasoning gap, caption benefits, CoT effects, and human–model performance gap are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the anonymous abstract link with a named GitHub repository, but abbreviates the VQA-generation prompt in Figure 12 and omits classification-prompt inputs and the output schema from Appendix H. Table 10 also shortens GPT-4o's precise snapshot identifier to GPT-4o-20. These are documentation/access changes, not established method changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work narrative remain unchanged. The benchmark comparison moves from v2 Table 5 to v3 Table 1 and adds question counts plus definitions of originality and validation, modestly extending the comparison with prior benchmarks.

P1.justification: V3 substantially condenses and rewrites the abstract and introduction, retitles the paper, and reorganizes its narrative. Existing metric validation and human-performance material become main-text sections, while limitations, risks, and reproducibility receive dedicated appendices.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout, merges captioning/open-ended result tables, replaces the correlation table with a radar chart, converts existing prompt boxes into numbered figures, and relocates several displays. Four subdiscipline tables are added. Some updated highlighting is incorrect: Table 5 marks Gemini-3-Flash's BLEU 2.46 as best despite a listed 2.52.

improvement.justification: Newer-model comparisons and subdiscipline breakdowns make the evaluation more informative, and existing human validation becomes easier to locate. However, v3 removes reproducibility details from prompts and introduces misleading result highlighting. These evidence-supported gains and losses leave the net direction of overall paper quality uncertain.
